system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Threshold note:** The Seller's preamble asserts its positions are "market standard", "settled at principal level", "agreed" and "FINAL". Under playbook sec 0.4/6.3, none of that is accepted. We have no record of any principal-level agreement and no Amelia Frost written authority for any fallback. Treat every position below as open and the draft as a first Seller mark-up.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback but no Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft exists, so it is not cleared.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and convert the basket into a deductible, materially shrinking recoverable loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl 12.3/13).
- Buyer wants: 24 months after Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject; hold at 24 months.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval, which has not been given.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity"; any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Collapsing title/capacity into the general regime would cap our recovery for a defective title at 20% of price with an 18‑month window – commercially unacceptable.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert an express, non-waivable carve-out.** This is a no‑exceptions playbook position and the Seller's drafting purports to limit liability even for fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sched 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- Buyer wants: only specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject general disclosures 1.1 and 1.2; require a fair-disclosure standard.** Whole-data-room disclosure would neutralise most warranties given the room's known gaps (see DL 2–10).

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete the blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer persons (and seller warranties qualified only by named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry); never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" standard is effectively a constructive-knowledge bar that, combined with N‑006, would gut the warranty package.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence conditions under cl 11.3 are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: effective Bluefen consent AND evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject; make effective consent plus condition-satisfaction evidence a CP.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m) and reasonable endeavours/consent-on-delivery gives us no protection if conditions remain unmet.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion (cl 2/7). DL 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge included.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release; require payout letter, funds-flow repayment and releases at Completion.** A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval, neither of which exists.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. DL 5 confirms exclusion and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded (e.g. Debt/transaction-cost deduction).
- Recommendation: **Reject; require explicit treatment and Seller confirmation of on-costs.** A debt-free/cash-free price cannot silently leave Completion-triggered liabilities in the Company.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL 4 notes AUD 180,000 open per DD-010, no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering title to and infringement/loss relating to SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving the cl 7.3 cure (payment triggers transfer); AUD 180,000 treated as unverified either way.
- Recommendation: **Reject as drafted; broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion payment and confirmatory assignment, or Seller funding.** Under DD-004 cl 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 IP until every fee clears, so a payment-only indemnity does not cover the ownership risk.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: DD-006 is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sched 6). DL 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification status undetermined; no breach admitted.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, written updates through Completion, warranty/indemnity cover for the incident; no assumption of breach, harm or notification duty, and no numeric demand yet.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept the materiality characterisation; require preservation, investigation and update covenants and a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident.** The Seller's own disclosure confirms the facts are unresolved, so "not material" is an assertion, not a finding.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL 8 cannot confirm whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: assessment of DD-008/DD-011 read together for timing and scope; classification decided on facts.
- Recommendation: **Reserve position; request the renewal terms, timing and accrual status before accepting "ordinary course".** No automatic Debt classification or price deduction is warranted, but equally the Seller's label is unverified.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13; 9.3/12.8/20.5); Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities as separate categories with their own regimes; no general-regime override.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert express category-separation language and an override clause in the Buyer's favour.** The Seller's "unless expressly stated otherwise" default is a hidden general-regime override that would capture every specific protection we negotiate.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. DL 10 confirms this is a Seller-supplied source and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extracts, share certificates/transfer history, PPSR and encumbrance searches, Seller board/authority documents, and Riverlark release (see N‑009).
- Recommendation: **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; run independent searches and require title/encumbrance/authority warranties under the fundamental regime.** An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP positions "settled" under the general regime.
- Buyer wants: terms remain OPEN; separate tax indemnity/warranty regime and IP regime to be negotiated; no assumption of unlimited liability.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "settled" characterisation; record Tax and IP as open items.** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process and folding them into the general regime would combine with N‑001/003/014 to cap and time-bar them.

---

**Overall:** No position in the Seller draft should be accepted as agreed, final or pre-cleared. Suggested next steps: (1) confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback authorities have been given; (2) issue a Buyer mark-up on the above; (3) send DD requests on Bluefen cl 11.3 conditions, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment/assignment, bonus on-costs, DD-006 investigation status, Sandbar terms and independent title searches.
=== END ADVICE ===
